hints: Think about what the two test reagents tell you, Na reacts with both alcohols and carboxylic acids, but Na2CO3 only reacts with acids.
Since X fizzes with Na but not with Na2CO3, it must contain an alcohol OH group and no CO2H group, so narrow it to a hydroxy ester.
Now check chirality by looking for a carbon with four different groups attached, only one of the hydroxy esters has this.
walkthrough:
**Use the chemical tests to find the functional groups**

Great start, let us decode the observations. Both $-OH$ and $-CO_2H$ give $H_2$ with Na, but only $-CO_2H$ gives $CO_2$ with $Na_2CO_3$.

$$\text{R-OH + Na} \rightarrow \text{H}_2 \text{ bubbles, } \text{R-CO}_2\text{H + Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 \text{ bubbles}$$
Since X bubbles with Na but not with $Na_2CO_3$, it has an alcohol group but no carboxylic acid group.

**Sort esters from acids**

This is the key filter. With formula $C_5H_{10}O_3$ containing three O atoms, the no-acid molecule must be a hydroxy ester, not a hydroxy acid.

Options A and B contain $CO_2CH_3$ (ester) plus $OH$ (alcohol). Options C and D contain $CO_2H$ (carboxylic acid) and would fizz with $Na_2CO_3$, so they are out.

**Check for exactly one chiral centre**

Remember, chiral means a carbon joined to four different groups. Look carefully at the middle carbons.

In $HOCH_2CH(CH_3)CO_2CH_3$, the $CH$ is bonded to $H$, $CH_3$, $CH_2OH$ and $CO_2CH_3$, four different groups, so it is chiral. This fits all the data perfectly.

options.A: Has the correct functional groups (alcohol plus ester) so it would pass the Na tests, but the central C is bonded to two identical $CH_3$ groups, plus $OH$ and $CO_2CH_3$. With only three different groups it is achiral, so it has zero chiral carbons, not one.
options.B: Correct on both counts. It is $HOCH_2CH(CH_3)CO_2CH_3$, a hydroxy ester with no $CO_2H$, so it gives $H_2$ with Na but no reaction with $Na_2CO_3$. The $CH(CH_3)$ carbon is attached to $H$, $CH_3$, $CH_2OH$ and $CO_2CH_3$, four different groups, giving exactly one chiral centre.
options.C: This is $CH_3CH_2C(CH_3)(OH)CO_2H$, a hydroxy carboxylic acid. The $CO_2H$ group would release $CO_2$ bubbles with $Na_2CO_3$, contradicting the observation. It is also achiral at the tertiary alcohol carbon because two alkyl groups are similar in a way that fails the test, but the acid test alone rules it out.
options.D: This is $CH_3CH(OH)CH(CH_3)CO_2H$, also a hydroxy carboxylic acid, so it would fizz with $Na_2CO_3$ and is ruled out. It is a trap because it does contain chiral carbons, but the functional group test fails first, so it cannot be X.
